about: Read by bin/hardcode-lint.sh (the hard-code lint, K12/D47) and its selftest bin/hardcode-lint-selftest.sh; names that look like a profile, model, provider, board, host or channel name but are not stack data. scan: patterns of the files to scan, whole paths where * stops at a folder border and ** crosses folders (the shipped list is every file); the lint scans every file git tracks (a walk of the root where there is no git) that matches scan and no skip row. skip: files left out, each with its reason (run_by: the file whose `for <name> in <words>;` list must hold the stem the row's first * matched, so only selftests the suite runner runs are left out; a word elsewhere in that file does not count). plain_words: role names that are ordinary words of the language, not counted as literals. own_names: the stack's own names (data folder, tool and marker names), one word-like token of 4 or more characters each, removed at word borders in every file before counting; a text may hold a literal joined to the rest by `.` or `-` (it then removes only that joined spelling, a bare use elsewhere still counts), never one glued to letters, digits or `_`. allow: exact text removed before counting in one file (where the word comes from, and the phase that may remove it). baseline: at most `count` whole-word uses of `literal` in `file`, each with the phase that removes it; a file and literal once; one more use, or a new literal, fails the suite. watch: literals no data file holds yet (other channels, Claude model names), counted like the data literals (B2V-05).

skip.why: a selftest the suite runner lists plants names to prove the lint and the guards; its own fake names are not stack code (a file of that name the runner does not list is scanned)
this file: it holds the names it excuses
the contract data files and schemas: the literals live here by design
the role table: the profile and role names live here by design
data: the alert texts, which name channels and tools
data: the fallback runner settings, which name its models
the limits file (ALERT_TARGET lives here by design) and runtime state
prose at the top of the repo (rules, plan, decisions): documents, not code the stack runs
prose: operator documents, not code the stack runs
fixtures: small projects the benchmark hands to a model; their words are test data
installed packages, not the stack (not tracked; a walk of a tree without git would meet them)
scratch work trees and copies, not the stack (not tracked)

plain_words.why: the root profile's name, which the agent runtime owns (Hermes's own word), and a common word
a common word of the language (the worker that builds); the role table names it, the profiles are builder-claude and builder-local, which are counted
a common word of the language (the one that sends work on)
a common word of the language (the verb)
a common word of the language (one who checks)
a common word of the language (not on a list)

own_names.why: the stack's data folder, where the contract data lives; not the project slug of the same name
the SOUL region marker, the stack's name, not the project slug
the apply tool's own file name (bin/stella-apply.py), not the project slug
the data tool's selftest name in bin/selftests.sh (bin/stella-data-selftest.sh), not the project slug
the recovery script's file name in docs/

allow.why: the argument name of Hermes's kanban_request_review tool (tools/kanban_tools.py), not a profile name
